title: Validate PostHog UUIDT ids by shape only; zod .uuid() rejects them
answers: workflow run cancel button fails with a validation error
cancel invocations API returns 400 for invocation_ids from the runs list
why does z.string().uuid() reject our invocation ids
how to validate a UUIDT in zod
body:
Symptom: An operator clicks Cancel on a running workflow, or calls the cancel API with `invocation_ids`. The request fails with a validation error and the run keeps going.
Root cause: nodejs/src/cdp/cdp-api.ts:CdpApi checked each id with zod's `z.string().uuid()`, which also checks the RFC version and variant. The invocation store issues UUIDTs. In a UUIDT those nibbles hold a series counter and random bytes, so the check rejected every real id.
Fix pattern: check the shape only with `z.string().refine((id) => UUID.validateString(id, false), msg)`. Keep the shape check: `cancelJobs` binds the ids as `::uuid[]`, so a malformed id must get a 400 at the route and never reach Postgres, where it would cause a 500. On the Python side Django's `UUIDField` already accepts UUIDTs. Do not add a version-aware check to the Django cancel serializer.
Constraints: this applies to any id generated as a UUIDT (posthog.uuidt.UUIDT / nodejs UUIDT). Per the PR, nodejs/src/cdp/schema/hogflow.ts still uses the version-aware rule for `message_category_id` and `template_uuid`, which are also UUIDT-backed. That is a known latent bug of the same kind and was not fixed here. Tests should use real `new UUIDT()` / `str(UUIDT())` ids. A `uuid4` passes either rule and hides this bug.
applies: Any zod/serializer validation of ids generated as PostHog UUIDTs, especially the CDP hog_flow invocations cancel route
